method: Sources found on PubMed Central; title, authors, journal, year, DOI, PMID, findings and limitations read from the article pages.

claims.claim: جسمك يخسر الدهون عندما يصرف طاقة أكثر مما يأكل (العجز الحراري).
claims.source_title: Quantification of the effect of energy imbalance on bodyweight
claims.authors: Hall KD, Sacks G, Chandramohan D, Chow CC, Wang YC, Gortmaker SL, Swinburn BA
claims.study_type: Mathematical model of energy balance, validated against controlled studies
claims.population: Adults; validated with data from CALERIE, inpatient liquid-diet and fasting studies
claims.main_finding: Changes in body weight and fat follow the balance between energy intake and expenditure; a sustained deficit draws down the body's energy stores.
claims.limitations: Assumes full adherence; individual baseline expenditure is uncertain (about 5%); effects of exercise on body composition are not modelled.

claims.claim: كلما نقص وزنك، قلّ ما يحرقه جسمك كل يوم، فالعجز الذي نجح في البداية قد يصغر مع الوقت.
claims.source_title: Quantification of the effect of energy imbalance on bodyweight
claims.authors: Hall KD, Sacks G, Chandramohan D, Chow CC, Wang YC, Gortmaker SL, Swinburn BA
claims.study_type: Mathematical model of energy balance, validated against controlled studies
claims.main_finding: Resting metabolic rate and the energy cost of physical activity fall as weight drops, so the deficit from an unchanged diet shrinks and weight loss slows; the static 3500 kcal rule overestimates later loss.
claims.limitations: Same model limitations as poc1-c1; this is one of several reasons weight loss can slow (others include water shifts and changes in adherence), which the script reflects with «أحد الأسباب» and «قد».

claims.claim: تناول بروتينًا كافيًا، ومارس تمارين المقاومة لحماية عضلاتك أثناء خسارة الوزن.
claims.source_title: Preserving Healthy Muscle during Weight Loss
claims.authors: Cava E, Yeat NC, Mittendorfer B
claims.population: Adults losing weight, including older adults with obesity
claims.main_finding: Adequate, not excessive, protein helps preserve lean mass during weight loss; resistance exercise preserves muscle mass and improves strength. Recommends a hypocaloric diet with adequate protein plus resistance training.
claims.limitations: Narrative rather than systematic review; the protein effect on fat-free mass is small (about 0.4-0.8 kg) and inconsistent; very high protein may blunt metabolic improvements.

claims.source_title: Practical inference from poc1-c2 (Hall et al., 2011)
claims.study_type: Practical recommendation derived from the model, not a tested protocol
claims.main_finding: Because expenditure falls as weight is lost, the intake that created a deficit at the start may not do so later.
claims.limitations: 'Every few weeks' is a practical interval, not one tested in a trial.
